title: What is a Qubit?
explanation: A normal computer uses bits: 0 or 1. A qubit is the basic unit of a quantum computer and can behave differently from an ordinary bit.

challenges.prompt: Which one is the basic unit of a quantum computer?

title: Measuring a Qubit
explanation: Measuring a qubit gives a result we can observe. If we run the same experiment many times, the results settle into a probability pattern.

challenges.prompt: A qubit starts at |0⟩ and no gates are applied. What will you see when you measure it?

title: The X Gate — Flipping a Qubit
explanation: The X gate flips a qubit. It changes 0 into 1 and 1 into 0.

title: Superposition — Being in Two States at Once
explanation: The H gate creates superposition: roughly equal chances of measuring 0 or 1.

title: Playing with Superposition
explanation: Applying H twice in a row cancels out — you end up back where you started, not in superposition.

challenges.prompt: Apply H, then H again, to |0⟩. What will you measure?

title: The Z Gate — The Invisible Flip
explanation: Z changes phase, not the 0/1 value directly — but combined with H, that hidden phase change becomes visible in the final measurement.

challenges.prompt: Apply H, then Z, then H to |0⟩. What will you measure?

title: Combining Gates on One Qubit
explanation: Gate order matters. Fix this broken circuit so it correctly creates a 50/50 superposition from |0⟩ — someone accidentally left an extra X gate in it.

challenges.prompt: This circuit is broken: X, X, H. Fix it so it produces a clean 50/50 superposition.

title: Two Qubits — Working Together
explanation: Two independent qubits can each be set separately — no connection between them yet.

challenges.prompt: Make both qubits become 1 (two independent qubits, no connection between them).

title: The CNOT Gate
explanation: CNOT is a controlled gate — the target qubit flips only when the control qubit is 1.

challenges.prompt: Set qubit 0 to 1, then use CNOT (control = qubit 0, target = qubit 1) so qubit 1 flips too.

title: Creating Entanglement
explanation: Entangling two qubits with H + CNOT produces strongly correlated results: mostly 00 and 11.

challenges.prompt: Build a Bell state: two qubits that produce mainly 00 and 11.

title: Exploring Different Entangled States
explanation: Not all entangled states look the same. This time, build one that produces mainly 01 and 10 instead of 00 and 11.

challenges.prompt: Build a circuit where the two qubits produce mainly 01 and 10 (opposite values, strongly correlated).

title: Interference — Making Probabilities Change
explanation: Phase (from the Z gate) doesn't show up directly in a measurement, but it can combine with later gates to force a specific outcome — this is interference.

challenges.prompt: Apply H, Z, H, Z to |0⟩, in that order. What will you measure?

title: Your First Real Quantum Algorithm — The Quantum Detective
explanation: A mystery function takes 0 or 1 and gives back an answer. Your job: figure out if it's constant (same output both times) or balanced (different outputs).

challenges.prompt: f(0) = 1 and f(1) = 1. Is this function constant or balanced?
f(0) = 0 and f(1) = 1. Is this function constant or balanced?

title: Mixing Everything You Learned
explanation: Combine gates across two qubits: lock one qubit to a definite value while the other stays in superposition.

challenges.prompt: Make qubit 0 definitely 1, while qubit 1 stays in a 50/50 superposition.

title: Free Practice & Creative Mode
explanation: Open sandbox — build any circuit you like with X, H, Z, and CNOT, and see what happens. No grading here, just experimenting. Ask Bloch if you want ideas.

title: Final Chapter — Quantum Architect (Boss Project)
explanation: Design a complete two-qubit circuit from scratch with minimal hints. Prove you understand gates, superposition, and entanglement together.

challenges.prompt: Build a circuit where the two qubits produce mainly 01 and 10 (opposite, strongly correlated) — no step-by-step guidance this time.
